texts: I travelled to six countries hunting for peace, and my arrow kept missing, then my grandmother said sit quietly and look at what is already in you.
You loose your arrow at far horizons, wanderer, yet the mark you seek was always standing in your chest.
arrow, search within
doha on shooting the arrow outward when the target is inside me
Write a doha about the seeker who sends his arrow farther and farther out, across every land, only to learn that what he was aiming at lay quietly inside himself the whole time.
doha: stop looking at the crossroads and the sun for God, look inside
crossroads, sun, look within
Do not wait at the crossroads for the rising sun to hand you the truth; the dawn you seek breaks inside.
Compose a verse about the pilgrim who stands at every crossroads and faces the sun in every direction, asking where God may be found, never turning his gaze inward where the answer waits.
I stood at a crossroads at sunrise for years asking for a sign, and no sign came until I closed my eyes and listened within.
Write a doha about the one who climbs every mountain to find the truth, exhausted at the top, and finds it only when he comes back and sits quietly inside himself.
mountain, answer within
After weeks of trekking up the mountain to find clarity, I came back and found it in a quiet corner of my own mind.
doha on climbing the mountain for answers but they were inside
You climb the mountain peaks in search, and the summit holds only wind; what you seek lives in the valley of your own heart.
look within, not without
O seeker, why do you wander the whole wide world? What you want rests within your own quiet.
i keep looking everywhere for peace, doha pls
Give me a verse about the person who searches every place, every book, and every teacher for peace, and finally discovers it is not found outside but only in the quiet room within.
I changed cities, jobs, and friends hoping to feel complete, and in the end it was a quiet evening alone that showed me what I had been missing.
Write a verse about the man who wears the forehead mark and acts like a thief of truth, snatching at doctrines and rituals outside himself, while the real treasure lies untouched in his own heart.
thief, forehead mark, search within
My uncle wears a forehead mark and keeps stealing wisdom from every guru he meets, never sitting with his own silence.
doha about a thief hunting outside for what is inside him, forehead mark too
The thief searches every pocket but his own; the forehead mark proclaims what the seeker has yet to find inside.
Compose a doha about the sadhu who covers himself with ash and travels from place to place seeking the divine, never realising that what he longs for is quietly waiting inside the one who seeks.
Ash on the forehead, ash on the arms, the seeker smears himself with the world; yet what he wants is clean within.
ash, look inside
My neighbour spends his savings on pilgrimages and ash-smeared rituals, but when he sits alone he never asks a single question of himself.
doha on smearing ash outside, but the answer is inside
doha on stop searching outside
turn inward
Why ask a thousand voices when your own is open? Turn your eyes inward and listen.
Years of reading scriptures got me nowhere, and then one night I just sat in silence and felt closer than ever to what I was after.
Write a verse for the one tired of seeking in teachers, books, and holy places, urging him to turn the search inward at last, because the thing he has been looking for has always been right there.
doha about how the answer is inside us not out there
My friend goes from retreat to retreat looking for happiness but never takes ten minutes to be alone with himself.
Compose a doha about the foolishness of running after truth in distant places when the one thing that matters lies silently in the quiet, hidden depths of the seeker's own being.
What you chase across the world rises from your own heart; breathe in, and be still.
search within
Write a verse about the seeker who scours the whole world for the beloved, unaware that the beloved is closer than his own breath, hidden in the secret chamber of his own heart.
I kept texting people for validation at midnight, and when I put my phone down and sat in the dark I found what I was missing.
something about looking inside yourself instead of everywhere else
Closer than breath, nearer than thought, he waits in your heart while you search the world.
beloved is within
boat, gold, inner treasure
Write a doha about the sailor who crosses every distance in his boat, hunting for gold on foreign shores, while the greatest treasure sits quietly in his own heart, which he never thought to open.
Gold in the boat's belly does not know it is rich; the sailor seeks treasure on every shore while it rides within.
doha on a boat with gold looking for treasure far away
My uncle sailed his boat to four countries to make his fortune, then came back and said the richest thing was inside him the whole time.
At every inn you ask, where is the Lord? The keeper smiles: He is the one who asks.
inn, search within
I stayed at a dozen guesthouses on my spiritual tour and the best answer I got was from the old keeper, who said look inside.
Compose a verse about the wanderer who stays at every inn along the road asking for the Lord, and is told by the wise old keeper that the guest he seeks lives inside the wanderer.
doha on checking into every inn to find God but he's inside
doha about wearing a cloth sheet and looking outside when the answer is within
Wrap yourself in a cloth sheet of holiness, wander from land to land; the Beloved waits unwrapped inside.
My cousin gave up his job, wrapped himself in a plain cloth sheet, and went wandering, and he called me to say that the answer had been in his room all along.
Write a doha about the seeker who dons a saffron cloth sheet, wanders from place to place looking for truth, and only discovers at the end of his journey that it was sitting quietly in his own heart.
cloth sheet, look within
close eyes, find within
What the eyes fail to find in a thousand places, the closed eyes find in one breath within.

Give me a verse about how the seeker, tired of running after teachers and rituals, finally closes his eyes, turns his attention inward, and finds in the stillness everything he travelled so far to find.
After a day of chasing answers, I closed my eyes on the train and found a stillness in me that no destination had ever given.
doha on how shutting my eyes shows more than traveling
At the crossroads you ask the road and ask the stranger; ask the quiet voice within, which knows.
crossroads, inner way
doha on the crossroads and looking inward
Compose a verse about the person standing at a crossroads of life, asking each passing stranger which way to go, who finally hears the answer when he stops asking others and listens inward.
When I was deciding whether to quit my job, I asked everyone I knew, and the answer only came when I sat still and asked myself.
I kept sipping advice from every self-help book like drops of dew, and nothing filled me until I sat down and asked myself what I truly wanted.
The seeker licks the dew from far-off leaves; the spring that quenches him wells up inside.
dew, inner depths
Write a doha about the thirsty seeker who gathers dew drop by drop from distant fields, never noticing the endless spring of peace that rises silently from the depths of his own being.
doha: the thirst isn't quenched by dew outside, it's within
In the market of the world you ask each stall for the jewel; open your own pocket, O fool, and find it.
Write a verse about the buyer who wanders the market asking every stall for the jewel of peace, paying for every promise, only to find it is already sitting unnoticed within his own heart.
market, treasure within
I went from shop to shop in the market looking for a gift that would fix my mood, then realized I needed to look inward instead.
doha on looking in the market for what is in me
I've fasted, walked barefoot, and bowed at every holy site, and only today did I notice how still it gets when I sit by myself.
Write a doha that tells the devotee who runs from one holy place to another that the Lord is found inside the seeker's own heart and that all his running is a detour.
doha on seeking god within
seek within
You wander every land and ask every teacher for a glimpse; the sacred place is open within you.
i need a doha on the crossroads and the inner road
Four roads leave the crossroads, and the seeker takes them all; the fifth road, within, he never tries.
Compose a verse about the wanderer who tries every road from the crossroads in search of God and returns tired, only to discover the fifth road, the road that leads inward, was open all along.
I took every path life offered at the crossroads of my twenties, and the one that finally led somewhere was the quiet one that went inward.
crossroads, look inward
doha about looking for god in ash and ritual but he's within
You smear the ash and chant aloud, yet the Lord whispers within; hush, and you will hear him.
ash, inward turn
A pilgrim in ash begged outside the holy place for a sign, and a little girl told him God was in his chest.
Write a doha about the ascetic who covers himself in ash and chants loud mantras on the road, and who is gently told by a child that the one he calls to is already listening inside him.
doha on chasing a scent that comes from me
Write a verse about the seeker mad with longing for a sweetness he follows down every path, never noticing that it rises from the depths of his own being.
Mad with longing, the seeker runs to the ends of the earth, never guessing the sweetness comes from within.
I chased success in every field, gave up many nights, and found that the contentment I wanted was there when I stopped.
scent from within
doha: blind man looks for philosopher's stone everywhere
blind man, philosopher's stone, within
My blind neighbour told me the philosopher's stone is not found in far places but in the quiet of one's own mind, and he said it with a smile.
Write a doha about the blind man who searches every shore for the philosopher's stone, only to learn that what he was looking for is hidden in his own body, waiting for him to turn inward.
The blind man searches the whole world for the philosopher's stone and wears it round his own neck.

Write a verse about the seeker who follows a thread of devotion inward, past thoughts and fears, until he finds the lotus blooming silently in the centre of his own heart, long before he began to look.
doha on following the thread to the lotus inside
Follow the thread inward and the lotus opens; follow it outward and it only tangles.
I pulled at the loose thread of my restlessness one night, and it led me inward to a place in me as peaceful as a lotus.
thread, lotus, inner search
A frantic week of googling answers ended when I turned off the screen and just sat quietly with my own thoughts.
Be still, still as an unmoved breath, and the question dissolves into the answer within.
Compose a verse for the one who has searched through books and teachers for truth, urging him to simply sit in silence, look inward, and discover the answer that all along lay waiting in him.
sit in silence, look in
gimme a doha about meditating to find answers
doha on the elephant going over every mountain but the answer is inside
elephant, mountain, search within
Write a doha about the mighty elephant that climbs mountain after mountain in search of the precious thing, only to realize it carried the treasure within, as every seeker does.
My strong, stubborn uncle crossed every mountain in the country looking for answers, and then said the biggest peak he climbed was the one inside him.
The elephant crosses every mountain for the sweet fruit, not knowing the sweetness is in its own heart.
doha on a bridge and ash and looking inside
After the funeral I crossed a bridge to scatter ash, and on the way back I felt the answer I wanted was inside me, not across the far shore.
Ash from the pyre, a bridge to the farther shore; but the shore you seek is in the chest of the crosser.
ash, bridge, inner shore
Compose a verse about the seeker who crosses bridge after bridge in search of the far shore and smears ash of renunciation on himself, only to find that the far shore was inside his heart.
palanquin, dew, within
My grandmother insisted on being carried in a palanquin to every holy place, and in her last year she said the dew she was hunting had been in her all along.

Write a doha about the pilgrim who travels in a palanquin to distant holy places, seeking the dew of divine grace, and who is gently reminded by the bearers that grace gathers inside the heart of the seeker.
Carried in a palanquin to far-off holy places, the dew of grace was already in the heart's own quiet.
doha on the palanquin and dew, inner search
the answer is inside
Seek not the Lord in far places, nor in closed pages; seek him in the silence that is yours.
doha for someone who has tried everything and still feels lost

Give me a verse about the seeker who has read every scripture and met every master, yet still feels empty, and who is finally taught that the one thing worth finding can be found only by looking inside.
I've done yoga, therapy, retreats, and books and still felt hollow, until one afternoon I sat with myself without trying to fix anything.
Ask not the stranger and ask not the crowd; ask the heart, for it has never lied to you.
doha on how i keep asking people instead of myself

Write a doha about the habit of asking everyone for advice and direction while the one truthful voice within us waits patiently to be heard, ready to answer the very questions we spend our lives asking others.
ask yourself
Before every decision I call five friends, and last month I finally asked myself first and found I already knew.
rope, temple, look within

Compose a verse about the devotee who pulls the rope at the temple to wake the Lord, who never thought to look into his own heart where the Lord had been waiting all along without the need for any rope.
My father pulled the rope at the temple every morning for years, and only in retirement did he say the real temple was the silence in him.
You tie a rope to the temple's gate, pull and shout; the Lord speaks softly within, unpulled.
doha on a rope and temple, God is within
gaze inward
Write a verse for the restless seeker whose eyes and feet always move outward, urging him to turn his gaze around and look at the one who is looking, where the search ends in a gentle surprise.
For years I went looking at faces for love, then one night I looked into my own eyes in silence and everything slowed down.
The seeker's eyes go out, and the seeker's feet go out; only the unmoving gaze within meets the Beloved.
doha on turning the gaze within
You carry water far for the holy bath and sit among skeletons for truth; the pot within holds the nectar.
pot of water, skeleton, inward
Write a doha about the seeker who carries a pot of water to holy sites and digs among skeletons in the cremation grounds, hunting for the truth, which lives inside the pot of his own body.
My uncle carried a pot of water to every holy site, and in a dry year he sat beside the village holy site and finally looked inward.
doha pot of water and skeleton, search within
Not far away, not in any distant place: he stirs in the breath you take.
I used to ask each night if anything was out there, and one night I noticed the strange stillness inside me.
Compose a doha telling the doubter who has looked everywhere for the divine that the Lord is neither far nor lost, but waits at the very centre of the seeker, who needs only to look inward.
doha: god is not in the sky, he's in me
where is God? within
winnowing fan, bier, within
doha on the winnowing fan and a bier, but the search is inside
The winnowing fan sifts husk from grain, but the bier is carried out empty if you never sift yourself.
My uncle judged every grain of everyone's life with a winnowing fan, and at the bier he realized he had never looked into himself.
Write a doha about the fool who sifts everyone else's grain with the winnowing fan and walks behind his bier without ever having sifted his own heart or asked what truth lay inside.
Milk holds butter in secret, unseen, and the seeker holds the Lord in secret, unfound until he churns himself.
Write a doha for the seeker who sees milk and knows the butter is hidden in it, and learns that the Lord is hidden in him the same way, found only by patient inward churning.
doha about milk and butter and God hidden inside
Watching my mother turn milk into butter, I understood that what I was looking for was hidden in me and needed only patience.
milk, search within
sandalwood, mirror, within
Compose a doha on the seeker who rubs sandalwood paste on his brow and stares into the mirror, yet never looks into the quiet mirror of the heart where his true face is seen.
I spend an hour at the mirror each morning applying sandalwood paste, yet never ten minutes asking who is the one looking back.
sandalwood and mirror doha on looking inward
The sandalwood does not smell its own fragrance until it is cut, and the seeker cannot see his own face till he looks in the mirror within.
doha on gold and pearl, treasure is within
The diver goes down for the pearl, the miser hoards his gold, and the true jewel burns unnoticed in his heart.
Write a verse about the seeker who dives for pearls and counts his gold, certain that happiness lies in some precious thing, and who learns late that the most valuable jewel was always inside.
gold, pearl, inner treasure
I chased gold and the pearl necklace dream for twenty years, and my happiest moment was an hour alone with my own thoughts.
I looked for happiness outside for years, any doha for that
Write a verse for the one who spent decades chasing happiness in other people, places, and possessions, and who learns at last that the source of lasting joy lay quietly in his own being all along.
After three failed relationships and two moves, I realized I'd been asking others to give me what I could find by looking inward.
happiness is inside
The thing you beg of the world is already yours; look within and receive it.
chakor bird, thread, inward
doha on the chakor bird looking at far thing but thread leads inward
The chakor bird stares at a distant glow, but the thread of love leads only to its own heart.
Compose a verse about the chakor bird that gazes toward a distant light, and the thread of longing that, if followed with care, leads the seeker not outward but back into his own quiet heart.
Like a chakor bird gazing at something far away, I admired teachers from a distance, until a thread of intuition led me back to myself.
Write a doha about the devotee who prays in mosque after mosque, travelling for blessings, and who is reminded that the true prayer is said in the quiet of the heart, where the Lord listens.
mosque, inner prayer
doha on searching in a mosque but it's inside
Every Friday I go to a different mosque hoping to feel something new, and what I felt most was the still moment alone after prayer.
In the mosque of every land the seeker kneels; the Beloved asks only that he kneel inside.
Compose a verse about the beggar who stretches out his bowl at every stranger, never realising that the greatest wealth lies inside him and needs no asking, only a turning inward.
The beggar begs at every gate, unaware that the richest wealth lies buried in his own chest.
beggar, treasure within
doha on a beggar looking outside for what is inside
A beggar outside my office said he had stopped asking people and started looking within, and he seemed happier than anyone I knew.
crow, search within
doha on a crow looking outside for what it needs
Write a doha about the crow circling all day above distant fields for its meal, and the seeker who flies everywhere for the truth, both forgetting that what they need can be found by turning inward.
The crow flies over every roof for a crumb; the seeker roams every land for a truth he carries inside.
Watching a crow circle for hours while I lay awake restless, it struck me that I too was hunting outside for what I carried.
house, hidden within
You search every corner of the house for the lost jewel; it is sewn into your own robe.
Write a verse about the man who turns over every room of his house hunting for a lost treasure, never thinking to look into his own heart where he left it long ago.
doha on looking everywhere in my house for something that is inside me
I turned my whole house upside down looking for a ring and realised that the real thing I had lost was my own sense of calm.
Give me a verse for the seeker who tires of running here and there for answers, and who finds on sitting quietly that the questions and the answers both rise within him.
look within, always
Why wander far when the beloved sits in your own silence, waiting for your gaze?
short doha on looking inward
For years I thought the answer was in another country, and then I spent a whole Sunday simply sitting with myself.
Compose a doha about the thief who steals from every stranger, always hungry for more, and who is finally told by an old man that the only wealth worth having cannot be stolen, only found within.
A man who used to steal told me that the happiest day of his life was the one when he sat in a prison cell and looked inside himself.
The thief breaks into a hundred strongboxes and leaves hungry, while the true treasure sits unlocked inside him.
thief, inner treasure
doha on a thief who finds the wealth was inside him
Quiet the senses one by one, and in the silence behind them meet the one you sought.
I switched off my phone and all the noise for a week and found someone in the silence who felt like an old friend.
doha about shutting out the world to find yourself
shut out, look in
Write a doha about the seeker who, tired of chasing all that glitters outside, quiets his senses one at a time and finds in the quiet within the meeting he has always wanted.
My grandfather planted a tree and said when I felt lost to remember that the tree draws strength from within the earth, not from the sky.
tree, roots within
doha: tree roots go inward, same for me
Compose a verse about the tree that stretches its branches toward the sky while its life flows from roots hidden below, teaching the seeker that his nourishment comes from the depths within.
The tree reaches for the sky but drinks from the roots; the seeker too must go down and in to be fed.
doha on a furnace and a tree, searching within
Write a verse about the furnace of spiritual practice that cannot compare with the inner glow, and about the tree whose real fruit is borne from within, to teach the seeker to look inward.
The furnace is lit outside the tree; the warmth that matters glows in the seeker's heart.
furnace, tree, inner warmth
I worked like a furnace for years under the shade of a promising career tree, and burned out until I looked to my inner life.
chakor bird, milk, within
Like a chakor bird I stared at far-off dreams, ignoring the cup of milk of contentment sitting beside me, which was really my own heart.
Compose a doha about the chakor bird that stares at the far glow and the cup of milk beside it untouched, and the seeker who forgets that the sweetness he wants sits patiently in his own heart.
doha on chakor bird and milk, find it inside
The chakor bird gazes upward and the milk lies unspilt beside it; the sweetness is inside the one who longs.
moneylender, look within
Our moneylender tracks every villager's debts and yet when I asked what he felt inside, he said he had never once looked.
The moneylender counts coins in other men's pockets; let him count the riches in his own breast.
doha on a moneylender counting everyone else's riches but his own
Write a verse about the moneylender who audits every neighbour's accounts, knows everyone's debts, but has never once taken stock of the quiet riches or the shadows within his own heart.
Write a doha about the seeker who bleeds on thorns in a faraway place looking for a diamond, only to find the flawless jewel was inside him from the start, safe from every thorn.
After years of painful journeys full of thorns, I found out that the diamond I wanted was a calm in me that no thorn could touch.
thorn, diamond, within
You cross a field of thorns for a diamond that lies glowing in your chest, unpricked.
doha on the thorn outside and the diamond inside
